impact.notes: Impact increases in hot paths, large inputs, high-concurrency services, build pipelines, or repeated request paths.

rules.name: Overprovisioned default Compose stack
rules.summary: Starting every service by default in local or default compose profiles wastes local compute and encourages unnecessary background activity.

impact.performance: Consumes memory and CPU that could be used elsewhere.
impact.carbon: Runs more services than needed for the task at hand.

rules.name: Unbounded restart loops for noncritical services
rules.summary: Restarting noncritical services aggressively can create needless churn and repeated work.

impact.cost: Consumes unnecessary local or CI resources.
impact.performance: Repeated restarts create churn and noise.

remediation.guidance: Use restart policies intentionally and avoid infinite restart churn for services that should fail fast during development.

rules.name: Missing multi-stage builds
rules.summary: Single-stage Docker builds often ship build tooling and temporary artifacts into runtime images, increasing image size and transfer cost.
rules.description: Dockerfiles that combine build and runtime concerns into a single final image increase storage, network transfer, cache churn, and deployment overhead.

impact.cost: Larger images cost more to store and move.
impact.performance: Slower pulls and startup in constrained environments.
impact.carbon: More bytes transferred and stored than necessary.

remediation.guidance: Separate build and runtime stages so only runtime assets ship in the final image.
examples: Use multi-stage builds with a builder stage and a minimal runtime stage.

pattern.title: Single-stage image with compiler toolchain
pattern.description: A runtime image includes package managers, compilers, and build caches that are only needed during build.

remediation.title: Split build and runtime stages
remediation.description: Build assets in one stage, then copy only the required runtime artifacts into a smaller final image.

rules.name: Oversized base image
rules.summary: Heavy base images increase transfer, storage, and patching footprint without improving runtime value.
rules.description: Using a large general-purpose base image when a smaller runtime image would suffice adds waste to build, deployment, and vulnerability management workflows.

impact.cost: Larger images cost more to store and distribute.
impact.performance: Longer image pull times delay startup.
impact.carbon: Unnecessary transfer and storage increase resource use.

remediation.guidance: Prefer minimal runtime images that still meet operational needs.
examples: Use slim or distroless images when practical and compatible with debugging and support needs.

rules.name: Missing or too-permissive .dockerignore
rules.summary: Large build contexts increase build time, cache churn, and unnecessary transfer to the Docker daemon.
rules.description: Without a properly scoped .dockerignore, source trees, artifacts, caches, and documentation may be copied into the build context even when they are not required for the image.

impact.cost: Larger contexts waste build and CI resources.
impact.performance: Builds become slower and less cache-friendly.
impact.carbon: Repeated transfer of unnecessary files increases waste.

remediation.guidance: Add and maintain a .dockerignore tuned to the actual files required for the build.
examples: Exclude node_modules, .git, test outputs, local caches, and generated artifacts unless explicitly needed.

rules.name: Package manager caches left in image layers
rules.summary: Leaving package indexes and caches behind increases image size with no runtime benefit.
rules.description: Docker image layers that retain apt, apk, pip, npm, or similar caches increase storage and transfer overhead while adding little or no runtime value.

impact.cost: Larger images increase storage and transfer cost.
impact.performance: Pulling and scanning images takes longer.
impact.carbon: Extra bytes are stored and transmitted repeatedly.

remediation.guidance: Clear package manager caches in the same layer where packages are installed, or use build-stage-only installs where possible.
examples: Combine install and cleanup in a single RUN instruction so caches do not persist into a committed layer.

rules.name: Build tooling shipped in runtime image
rules.summary: Runtime images should not carry compilers, package managers, or build-only tooling that is not needed after build.
rules.description: Shipping build-only tools in the final image increases image size and operational complexity while providing no runtime efficiency benefit.

impact.cost: Bigger runtime images cost more to move and store.
impact.performance: Extra image weight slows distribution and cold starts.
impact.carbon: Unnecessary runtime bytes increase repeated resource use.

remediation.guidance: Keep build tooling in dedicated builder stages and ship only runtime dependencies.
examples: Copy built binaries or packaged assets into a clean runtime stage.

rules.name: Missing or mis-sized CPU and memory requests and limits
rules.summary: Containers without realistic requests and limits create waste, contention, or throttling.
rules.description: Kubernetes workloads that omit or poorly size CPU and memory requests and limits make scheduling and capacity planning less efficient, increasing cluster waste and instability.

impact.cost: Poor sizing can lead to overprovisioning or noisy-neighbor contention.
impact.performance: Bad sizing increases throttling or eviction risk.
impact.carbon: Inefficient capacity use drives unnecessary cluster footprint.

remediation.guidance: Set realistic requests and limits based on actual workload behavior and revise them as measurements improve.
examples: Use observed workload baselines instead of copy-pasted defaults.

rules.name: Missing HPA for horizontally scalable workloads
rules.summary: Workloads that can scale horizontally but do not use autoscaling can waste cluster capacity or under-serve demand.
rules.description: When a workload is horizontally scalable, the absence of an HPA or equivalent scaling policy can lead to static overprovisioning or inefficient manual scaling.

impact.cost: Static replicas often overrun actual need.
impact.carbon: Idle replicas consume resources without corresponding value.

remediation.guidance: Use autoscaling where workloads and metrics support it, and tune target thresholds carefully.
examples: Deploy HPA for stateless services with clear CPU or custom metric signals.

rules.name: Overly aggressive health probes
rules.summary: Very frequent probes create unnecessary traffic and container work, especially at scale.
rules.description: Health probes that run more often than necessary or do expensive work can create avoidable load on applications and the cluster control path.

impact.cost: Probe overhead adds up across many pods.
impact.performance: Expensive probes can compete with application work.
impact.carbon: Repeated low-value probe traffic and execution waste resources.

remediation.guidance: Tune probe frequency and probe implementation so checks are lightweight and proportional to real operational need.
examples: Avoid high-frequency probes that trigger full dependency checks on every interval.

rules.name: Heavy or redundant sidecars
rules.summary: Sidecars add useful capabilities, but they also add CPU, memory, storage, and network overhead.
rules.description: Workloads that carry heavy or redundant sidecars for logging, metrics, proxies, or helpers can create duplicated per-pod overhead that scales poorly across clusters.

impact.cost: Per-pod overhead multiplies across replica counts.
impact.performance: Sidecars compete for pod resources and may add latency.
impact.carbon: Repeated duplicated overhead increases cluster resource use.

remediation.guidance: Use sidecars intentionally, consolidate where possible, and prefer shared platform capabilities when they reduce duplicated per-pod cost.
examples: Review whether the same capability can be provided once per node or per cluster instead of once per pod.

rules.name: Unpinned images using latest or floating tags

impact.carbon: Unnecessary image movement and deployment churn increase resource use.
